newsitem.title: USA: Ultramar sees jobs cuts from Total deal.
newsitem.headline: Ultramar sees jobs cuts from Total deal.

text.p: Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp expects its acquisition of Total Petroleum will result in an unspecified number of job cuts, the heads of both companies told reporters Tuesday in a telephone conference.
"Regrettably a number of employees will not be offered continued employment," said Roger Hemminghaus, chief executive of Ultramar Diamond.
He said those employees who lose their jobs will be offered severance packages. He did not elaborate.

"It's too early in the process to say how many people may not have jobs going forward," Hemminghaus said in response to a question. The answer to that question will grow more clear over the next three months, he said.
He noted the job cuts will be concentrated in area such as information technology or accounting.
"In these corporate-wide departments there will be consolidations," Hemminghaus said.
The $811 million deal gives Ultramar Total's three refineries located in Colorado, Oklahoma and Michigan, as well as Total's marketing assets concentrated in the southwest and Michigan.

With Total's three refineries with a total crude oil processing capacity of about 150,000 barrels per day (bpd), and its 710 company-owned and jobber-run retail outlets, the expanded Ultramar will have total crude processing capacity of 650,000 bpd and 6,381 branded outlets.
The expanded company will be based in San Antoniom, Texas, Ultramar's current home territory.
